title: Cutaneous leishmaniasis with ulcer and smear-confirmed amastigotes
text: A patient with an ulcerated plaque on the forearm after sandfly exposure had a lesion smear showing amastigotes. The presentation was consistent with localized cutaneous leishmaniasis.

title: Papulonodular skin lesion in endemic travel history
text: A chronic papule progressing to a nodular ulcer after endemic travel supported cutaneous leishmaniasis. Biopsy and PCR were used for confirmation.

title: Visceral leishmaniasis with prolonged fever and splenomegaly
text: Prolonged fever, weight loss, pancytopenia, and splenomegaly are classic features of visceral leishmaniasis. Bone marrow or tissue confirmation is typically required.

title: Kala-azar pattern with hepatosplenomegaly
text: Kala-azar often presents with hepatosplenomegaly, chronic fever, anemia, and systemic illness rather than an isolated skin ulcer.

title: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis with nasal and oral involvement
text: Nasal septal destruction, oral ulceration, and mucosal inflammation after prior cutaneous disease support mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.

title: Palatal and nasal mucosal disease in leishmaniasis
text: Palatal or nasal mucosal lesions with compatible epidemiology should raise concern for mucocutaneous leishmaniasis and prompt tissue confirmation.
